stem: Which section of the Constitution of Zimbabwe is mainly about the rights of persons with disabilities?

options.content: Section 83
options.rationale: Correct: it sets out measures for persons with disabilities.

options.content: Section 60
options.rationale: Section 60 is freedom of conscience and religion.

options.content: Section 78
Section 17

explanation: **Section 83** (with the national objective in section 22) concerns persons with disabilities. Section 60 is freedom of religion.

stem: Which of these is a form of reasonable accommodation for a learner who is blind?

options.content: Notes in Braille
options.rationale: Correct: it removes a barrier to reading.

options.content: Lessons in a hall with steps only
A louder bell at the end of lessons
Extra homework to complete at home
options.rationale: This does not remove the barrier.

explanation: **Braille** notes remove a barrier for a learner who is blind; other examples are large print and a reader.

options.content: Learners with disabilities stay at home until they are old enough to work
Learners with disabilities are always taught in a separate building
options.rationale: Separate schooling is not the definition.

options.content: Learners with disabilities may attend only on days when classes are small
Learners with disabilities learn in ordinary schools with support

explanation: **Inclusive education** brings learners with disabilities into ordinary classrooms with the support they need.

stem: What does section 56 of the Constitution of Zimbabwe guarantee?

options.content: The right to marry at any age
options.rationale: Section 78 sets the minimum age at 18.

options.content: Equality and freedom from unfair discrimination
options.rationale: Correct: it includes disability as a ground.

options.content: The right to own land in every district
The right to ignore the laws of the country

explanation: **Section 56** guarantees equality and forbids unfair discrimination, including on grounds of disability.

stem: Which of the following would make worship more inclusive for a member who is deaf?

options.content: A louder choir and a larger sound system for the hall
options.rationale: This does not help a person who is deaf.

options.content: A shorter service held on Sundays only
options.rationale: This does not address the barrier.

options.content: A rule that visitors should sit at the back of the hall
options.rationale: This does not address the barrier.

options.content: A sign-language interpreter or a printed service sheet
options.rationale: Correct: it removes the communication barrier.

explanation: A **sign-language interpreter** or printed text removes the barrier for a member who is deaf.

stem: Tatenda's mosque has steps at the only entrance and a member who uses a wheelchair cannot enter. Which response best applies the right to participation?

options.content: Ask the member to pray at home, since the building is old and cannot be changed
Tell the member that the steps are a test of patience in his faith
options.rationale: This places the problem on the person.

options.content: Install a ramp and a wide door so that the member can enter with everyone else
Wait until the member's family can pay for a different mosque to be built

explanation: A **ramp** and wide door remove the barrier and respect the right to take part in worship.
hints: Which answer removes the barrier now and keeps the member with the community?

stem: Why can laws alone fail to change the lives of people with disabilities?

options.content: Laws are never written down, so nobody can know what they say or find them
People with disabilities are not covered by the law of the country at all
Schools, communities and religious groups must put rights into practice
Laws are meant to apply only to religious organisations and not to schools

explanation: Rights in law become real only when **schools, communities and religious groups** put them into practice.
hints: Think about the gap between a right in law and daily life.

stem: Which statement best explains why inclusion is about rights and not only charity?

options.content: Charity is illegal in Zimbabwe, and only government may give help
People with disabilities have equal rights, so barriers should be removed, not only pitied
options.rationale: Correct: charity alone leaves unequal rights.

options.content: People with disabilities do not need help from anyone in their communities
Rights apply only to adults and children have only a right to charity

explanation: Inclusion means **equal rights** and removing barriers; pity alone treats people as objects of help.

stem: The UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities was adopted in 2006.
explanation: True. The Convention says that persons with disabilities have the same human rights as everyone else.

stem: Inclusive worship means giving people with disabilities a seat at the back and no other role.
explanation: False. Inclusive worship removes barriers and welcomes people with disabilities into the full life of the community.

stem: Match each adjustment with the barrier it removes.

right.content: pressure on a learner who needs longer
text that cannot be read by a person with low vision

explanation: Each adjustment removes a particular barrier.

payload.template: Section {{blank:a}} of the Constitution sets out the rights of persons with disabilities, and section {{blank:b}} guarantees equality.

explanation: Section **83** concerns persons with disabilities; section **56** guarantees equality.

stem: What number can a child call in Zimbabwe to report abuse to Childline?
explanation: **Childline Zimbabwe** can be reached on 116; other help channels include the police Victim Friendly Unit and a clinic.

stem: Identify **three** ways in which a school can include learners with disabilities.

points.description: Build ramps and accessible toilets
Provide Braille, large print or sign-language support
Train teachers and encourage classmates to include everyone

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A school can build ramps and accessible toilets, provide Braille, large print or sign-language support, and train teachers and encourage classmates to include everyone.

stem: Describe how religious organisations have helped people with disabilities in Zimbabwe.

points.description: Many special schools and centres began as church or mission projects
Some run clinics and rehabilitation centres
Religious groups give charity and raise funds
They teach dignity and can speak against myths and stigma

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Many special schools and centres began as church or mission projects, and some run clinics and rehabilitation centres. Religious groups give charity and raise funds, and they teach dignity and can speak against myths and stigma.

hints: Cover schools, health care, funds and teaching.

stem: Explain **two** challenges that religious organisations face in including people with disabilities.

points.description: Some buildings are not accessible
Developed: old churches or mosques with steps and narrow doors keep wheelchair users out, and rebuilding costs money
Some leaders and members still repeat myths
Developed: if disability is called a punishment or a curse, families are shamed and people stay away from worship

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Some buildings are not accessible: old churches or mosques with steps and narrow doors keep wheelchair users out, and rebuilding costs money. Some leaders and members still repeat myths, and if disability is called a punishment or a curse, families are shamed and people stay away from worship.

explanation: Two challenges, each stated (1) and developed (2).
hints: Give one challenge about buildings and one about attitudes.

stem:
**Source A** — an extract from a fictional community notice in Gweru, 2026 (invented for this question)

> The inter-faith youth forum met last Saturday. Members from a church, a mosque and a synagogue agreed to visit each place of worship and check access. They noted that the church has a ramp, the mosque has steps at the only entrance, and the synagogue has no large-print prayer books. They will ask the leaders of each community to make changes and will share their findings with the local council.

Study Source A and answer the questions.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: According to Source A, which place of worship has steps at the only entrance?

options.content: The church
The mosque
options.rationale: Correct: the forum noted steps at the mosque.

options.content: The synagogue
options.rationale: The synagogue lacks large-print prayer books.

options.content: The council office
options.rationale: The council office is not mentioned as a place of worship.

parts.explanation: The forum found that the mosque has steps at the only entrance.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Using Source A, state **three** findings of the youth forum.

points.description: The church has a ramp
The mosque has steps at the only entrance
The synagogue has no large-print prayer books

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The church has a ramp, the mosque has steps at the only entrance, and the synagogue has no large-print prayer books.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain how the forum's plan in Source A promotes inclusion.

points.description: It identifies barriers in each place of worship
It asks leaders to make changes, such as a ramp or large-print books
Members of different religions work together and share findings with the council

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The forum identifies barriers in each place of worship and asks leaders to make changes, such as a ramp or large-print books. Members of different religions work together and share their findings with the council.

explanation: The source shows an access audit and shared action.
hints: In (c) link finding, action and cooperation.

stem: Mthulisi says: "Laws are enough to protect people with disabilities." Nyasha says: "Laws help, but communities and religious groups must also change attitudes."

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Outline **two** rights of persons with disabilities in the Constitution of Zimbabwe.

points.description: A first right, stated accurately with the section or its meaning
indicators: Equality and freedom from unfair discrimination (section 56)
The State must promote the dignity and participation of persons with disabilities (section 22)
The State must take measures for self-reliance, protection from abuse and access to education and care (section 83)

points.description: A second right, different from the first
indicators: Any other right listed for the first point

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The Constitution guarantees equality and freedom from unfair discrimination (section 56). It also says that the State must promote the dignity and participation of persons with disabilities (section 22) and take measures to protect them from abuse and help them to learn and become self-reliant (section 83).

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain why accessible buildings are important for inclusion.

points.description: Barriers such as steps keep people with physical disabilities out of school and worship
Ramps and wide doors allow equal participation, which is a right and a sign of dignity

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Barriers such as steps keep people with physical disabilities out of school and worship. Ramps and wide doors allow equal participation, which is a right and a sign of dignity.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Assess the view that laws are the most important way of protecting the rights of people with disabilities.

points.description: For: laws set standards, give rights and allow people to claim them
Against: laws do not remove myths or barriers on their own; communities and religious groups carry out change
Link: laws and attitudes work together; religious teaching about dignity supports the law
A supported judgement

levels.descriptor: Developed explanation of several relevant points or arguments, supported by accurate, specific knowledge and examples, considering more than one side and reaching a supported judgement that answers the question.
Developed explanation of some factors or arguments with relevant supporting detail; a judgement is attempted but is only partly supported, or the other side is thin.
Some explanation of one or two relevant factors, or several points described with limited explanation; little or no judgement.
Simple, general or narrative statements with limited relevance to the question; little explanation.

answerSpec.modelAnswer: Laws set standards, give rights and allow people to claim them, so they are important. However, laws do not remove myths or barriers on their own, and communities, schools and religious groups carry out change by building ramps, teaching dignity and challenging stigma. Laws and attitudes work together, and religious teaching about dignity supports the law. I conclude that laws are essential but not the most important way on their own.

explanation: A strong answer weighs law against practice and concludes that both are needed.
hints: Weigh the power of law against the need for changed attitudes.
